resources.string: This divider is empty. Press the red button and speak - the recording lands right here.
One moment… the microphone is coming back
One moment… turning the microphone on
Without the microphone Tapedo can’t hear your note. Allow the microphone in the phone settings.
This phone has no speech recognition. Install or enable the Google app.
I didn’t hear anything. Press the button and say it again.
Speech recognition couldn’t reach the internet. Check the connection, or download the language for offline use in the phone’s speech recognition settings - then no internet is needed.
Speech recognition is busy with another app. Try again in a moment.
Something went wrong with the microphone. Try again.
Your phone did not accept gap-free recording, so Tapedo records the older way. Recording works, but a word may get lost after a pause.
Send the error - the author will fix it in the next version.
Send the error to the app’s author
Your mail app opens with a ready message: Tapedo version, phone model, Android version, language and the error code - no notes, no recordings. You send it yourself.
There is no mail app. The error report is on the clipboard - paste it into a message to %1$s.
The phone has no offline pack for this language, so nothing was sent. Online recognition sends your voice to Google. You can also download the offline pack in the phone’s speech recognition settings.
The phone has no offline pack for this language, and online recognition is turned off in Settings. Download the offline pack in the phone’s speech recognition settings.
%1$s ends the recording when you say nothing for a while. %2$s keeps listening until you press it. Short pauses to think never cut anything off.
This phone listens without breaks - pauses cut nothing off.
This phone restarts listening after a pause - go on when the pen is back on the paper.
After the first recording you will see here whether pauses interrupt listening.
This many seconds without new words ends the recording.
A pause starts a new item
This many seconds between words starts a new list item. “Never” - one recording (and each one added to a card) is one item.
A safety net for when you forget to stop.
The language you speak to the phone in. Tapedo’s own texts follow “Language” on the “Look” tab.
By default your voice stays on the phone. When the offline pack for the speech language is missing, Tapedo asks before sending your voice to Google.
On phones with on-device recognition (usually Android 12 and newer) your voice never leaves the phone without your consent. On others the system may go online by itself.
Note: this phone cannot recognise speech on the phone itself - the system may send your voice to Google by itself, without asking. Tapedo cannot block that.
Couldn’t save the change. Try again.
Makes the text in Tapedo bigger or smaller - on top of the text size set on the phone.
Paper - light, like an index card. Panel - dark, like a recorder’s case.
After “stop” Whisper types the recording once more, more exactly than the phone. While you speak, the phone still shows the words.

Whisper is a speech recognition model by OpenAI. Groq offers it free within a daily limit, OpenAI for about 0.006 USD per minute of recording (as of Nov 2026). Works on Android 13 and newer. The recording stays in the phone’s memory only, never on disk. When Whisper fails, the phone’s text stays and the window after the recording says why.
Where the data goes: after every recording the audio (without the countdown and the silence at the end) goes to %1$s. By picking %1$s you agree to that.
The %1$s key is saved - that is enough, the switch in the %1$s frame above is not needed.
No %1$s key - enter it above, in the %1$s frame. Until then the phone’s text stays.
Whisper - more exact typing of the recording by AI - is on the “AI” tab.
Cards and switches change instantly, without movement. Also on automatically when animations are off system-wide.
Cards, tapes and stamps lie slightly crooked, as if tossed on a desk.

Cards are encrypted and stored only on this phone. Tapedo never saves sound - only the text is kept. Nothing leaves the phone unless you allow it: the note text goes to the AI provider you choose, your voice goes to Google with online recognition, and the recording goes to Whisper when you turn it on.
Tapedo turns what you say into cards - notes, tasks, lists, shopping, events and ideas. No account, no ads and no server run by the author.
There is no mail app. The address %1$s is on the clipboard.
Tapedo is built from open source libraries and fonts. Their licences follow in their original wording.

AI splits a note into separate cards and lists, spots dates and fixes misheard words. Without AI, simple rules structure your notes: a shopping list after “buy”, an event after “at 10”, priority after “urgent”, a due date after “tomorrow” - it works offline and the note text never leaves the phone.

You can turn on several providers - Tapedo asks them in turn, in the order of this list. When one uses up its daily limit, the next notes go to the next one. When nobody answers, the no-AI rules structure the note.
The best of the free ones: decent and very fast, but misses subtleties. About 1000 requests a day per model (Nov 2026).
Very weak and makes things up (adds things that were never said) - a fallback only. “openrouter/free” picks a different model each time, so results are uneven. About 50 requests a day (Nov 2026).

The most accurate. Recommended: Claude Sonnet 5.5 - about 0.6 US cents per minute of recording (Nov 2026). Opus 5.5 costs twice as much, which is overpaying for sorting notes; the cheaper Haiku is wrong more often.
Default gpt-6-luna - cheap, but wrong more often. Key from the OpenAI platform.
Default Gemini Flash-Lite - cheap, but wrong more often. Google gives its free plan only to some accounts and projects. Key from Google AI Studio.
A service that runs open AI models very fast. It splits a note into separate tasks and lists. The free plan needs no payment card; it has per-minute and per-day request limits.
One account for many AI models from different companies. It splits a note into separate tasks and lists. Free models have “:free” in the name - about 50 requests a day without topping up.
Claude AI models by Anthropic. They split a note into separate tasks and lists. Paid per use - the account needs credit; with Sonnet 5.5 roughly 0.6 US cents per minute of recording (Nov 2026).
GPT AI models by OpenAI. They split a note into separate tasks and lists. Paid per use - the account needs credit.

Google’s AI model. It splits a note into separate tasks and lists and fixes misheard words. Google gives its free plan only to some accounts and projects - new projects usually work only with billing set up, which is why Gemini is paid here and last on the list. Adults only (18+).

Only the note text goes to Groq (USA) - no data about you; the recording only if you pick Groq for Whisper. Under its terms Groq may not use it to train models. By default it stores no requests; for outages it may keep logs for up to 30 days - this can be turned off in the Groq console (Data Controls, Zero Data Retention).

Only the note text goes to OpenRouter (USA) - no recording, no data about you. OpenRouter itself stores no requests unless you turn that on, but it passes them to the company running the model - with free models some of them may train on the text. Such models can be turned off in OpenRouter’s privacy settings; do not dictate sensitive data there (as of Nov 2026).

Only the note text goes to Anthropic (USA) - no recording, no data about you. Under its commercial terms Anthropic does not train models on API data and deletes requests automatically within 30 days - longer only for those flagged as breaking its rules (as of Nov 2026).

Only the note text goes to OpenAI (USA) - no data about you; the recording only if you pick OpenAI for Whisper. API data is not used to train models unless you opt in; OpenAI keeps it for up to 30 days to detect abuse (as of Nov 2026).

Only the note text goes to Google - no recording, no data about you. On the paid plan Google does not use it to improve its products and keeps it for a limited time only to detect abuse. On the free plan (if your project has one), outside the EEA, Switzerland and the UK, Google may use the text and let people read it - then do not dictate sensitive data (as of Nov 2026).
Tap “Create a key” - the Groq console opens. Create an account (e-mail, Google or GitHub).
In “API Keys” tap “Create API Key”, name it and copy the key - Groq shows it only once.
Paste the key below and tap “Check connection”. The free plan needs no card.
Tap “Create a key” - OpenRouter opens. Create an account.

In “Keys” tap “Create Key”. Under “Credit limit” choose “Custom amount” and enter 1 - it only caps what the key may spend; without topping up the account you pay nothing, and “:free” models cost 0. Copy the key - it is shown only once.
Pick a model with “:free” in the name - only those are free (about 50 requests a day without topping up). Paste the key below and tap “Check connection”.
Tap “Create a key” - the Claude console opens. Create an account.
In “Billing” add credit - without it the key does not work.
In “API keys” tap “Create Key”, copy the key (shown only once), paste it below and tap “Check connection”.
Tap “Create a key” - the OpenAI platform opens. Create an account.
In “Billing” add credit - without it the key does not work.
In “API keys” tap “Create new secret key”, copy the key (shown only once), paste it below and tap “Check connection”.
Tap “Create a key” - Google AI Studio opens. Sign in with a Google account.
On aistudio.google.com/billing set up billing for the project - without it Gemini works only in projects with a free plan (see the “Billing Tier” column; “Free tier unavailable” = paid only).
Tap “Create API key”, copy the key, paste it below and tap “Check connection”.
I keep the key encrypted in the phone’s vault (Android Keystore), never in a plain file, and send it only to this provider. The screen shows the last 4 characters, the whole key - after “Show key”.
The key is missing - without it AI does not work.
The daily limit from the settings is used up (requests: %1$d) - Tapedo asks again tomorrow.
%1$s says its daily limit is used up - Tapedo asks again tomorrow.
Empty = default: %1$s. Model names are on the provider’s site.
Getting the list from the provider…
Free models - tap one to pick it:
List saved in the app on 7 Nov 2026 - models change quickly, the provider has the current one.
The provider’s list is not available: %1$s Below is the list saved in the app.
One small request - it counts towards the daily limit.
Requests today: %1$d of %2$d, in the last 30 days: %3$d.
The amount of the last top-up of the Claude account, in dollars, as Anthropic counts. Type it in right after topping up: Tapedo counts spending from the day it is saved.
About %1$s PLN (about 4 PLN per $, Nov 2026). Spending counted from %2$s - after the next top-up, type in the new amount.
Type an amount in dollars, e.g. 5 or 20.50 (0.01 to 10000).
Spent since %1$s: about %2$s of %3$s, about %4$s left (about %5$s PLN).
Tapedo works this out itself from tokens and Claude’s price list (as of Nov 2026), so it is an estimate - the exact balance is in the Claude console, under “Billing”.
About %1$s of the %2$s Claude top-up is left - less than 10%%. Top up the account before Claude stops answering.
After topping up, type in the new amount above.
After topping up, type in the new amount in Settings, on the “AI” tab, under Claude.
After this many requests to one provider Tapedo waits until tomorrow - a free limit is never overrun.
All providers that are on wait until tomorrow - the no-AI rules structure the notes.
Notes go to the next provider on the list.
Only the note text goes to the AI that writes the cards - never the recording, keys, other cards or data about you. The recording goes only to Whisper (below), when you turn it on.
the key is invalid - check that it was copied whole, or create a new one.
the API is turned off in the provider’s project - turn it on there or create a key in a new project (see “How to get a key”).
this Google project has no free plan - Gemini works in it only with billing (aistudio.google.com/billing), and a new key in the same project will not help. Groq and OpenRouter stay free.
Google wants the project confirmed by phone - open Google AI Studio (“Create a key”) and verify, or turn on another free provider.
the provider refused this account or project - check its site (account, billing, e-mail notices) or turn on another provider.
the model does not exist or is not available for this account - pick another free model.

the model is busy at the provider for a moment (many people use the same free model, or a per-minute limit was hit) - not the daily limit. Tapedo asks it again with the next note; you can also pick another free model - on OpenRouter “openrouter/free” picks a free one itself.
the provider’s limit is used up - Tapedo asks again tomorrow, or right away after a model change.
the daily limit from the settings is used up - Tapedo asks again tomorrow.
the saved key could not be read - try again. The key is not lost; if this keeps happening, paste it again.
no connection, or the provider does not answer - check the connection.
the answer came empty or incomplete - try again or pick another model.
the provider reported an error - try later or turn on another provider.
the phone gave Tapedo no recording - Whisper works on Android 13 and newer, when the phone’s speech recognition takes Tapedo’s recording.
the recording is too long for Whisper (about 12 minutes at most in one recording).
Simple rules wrote these cards instead of the AI:
Whisper did not type the recording - the phone’s text was kept:
Couldn’t save the cards. Nothing is lost - try again.
Already saved - tap a card to change it. You can also record more or delete.
The same words once more to Claude Sonnet 5.5 - it splits them into cards and spots the types more accurately. The cards you have stay until you pick the new ones.
Claude did not write the cards - the ones you have stay.
Cards can’t be opened right now. Nothing was deleted - try again.
Couldn’t save the change. Try again.
The card is now behind the “%s” divider.

Android lost the key they were encrypted with (it can happen after a system update or a screen lock change), so Tapedo started with an empty stack. The encrypted files were not deleted - they stay in the app’s data, but nobody can read them without the key.
Say what to add to the list, e.g. “butter and eggs”.
What you say is added at the end of the text.
